rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice when “literally” is loose, informal emphasis or filler.

example.english: I’m literally so tired I want to sleep on the floor.
example.traditional: 我真係攰到想瞓喺地下。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zan1 hai6 gui6 dou3 soeng2 fan3 hai2 dei6 haa6

rows.note: Use this when “literally” means merely or just, especially to downplay how simple an action is.

example.english: I literally just asked, that’s all.
example.jyutping: ngo5 zi2 hai6 man6 haa5 ze1

rows.note: Use this for a strong, often figurative dramatising emphasis rather than a precise word-for-word claim.

example.english: It’s literally hot enough to fry an egg today.
example.traditional: 今日熱到直頭可以煎蛋。
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 jit6 dou3 zik6 tau4 ho2 ji5 zin1 daan6

rows.note: Use this when “literally” means according to the exact words or not figuratively.

example.english: Taken literally, this sentence isn’t a metaphor.
example.traditional: 呢句照字面睇，唔係比喻。
example.jyutping: ni1 geoi3 ziu3 zi6 min6 tai2 m4 hai6 bei2 jyu6
